## AI-generated Overview (from reference literature and SuttaCentral)
*This overview was drafted by an AI model from the cited scholarship and SuttaCentral data and may contain errors; verify against the sources before relying on it.*
The *Paṭhamanāvāvimānavatthu* ("Ship Mansion", Vv 6) is the sixth discourse of the *Vimānavatthu* in the Pali Khuddaka Nikāya [SuttaCentral]. In this narrative, the Arahant Mahāmoggallāna interrogates a female deity to discover the past meritorious actions that resulted in her rebirth in a celestial mansion characterized as a golden-roofed ship [SuttaCentral]. Six translations in six modern languages are recorded on SuttaCentral [SuttaCentral].
In terms of parallels and text reuse, SuttaCentral lists two full parallels in the subsequent *Vimānavatthu* discourses, *Dutiyanāvāvimānavatthu* (Vv 7) and *Tatiyanāvāvimānavatthu* (Vv 8), as well as a resembling parallel in the *Sāsanapaṭṭhāna* of the *Nettippakaraṇa* (Ne 37) [SuttaCentral]. Automated analysis by DharmaNexus indicates extensive Pali-internal text reuse across 27 texts (190 matching passages), agreeing with SuttaCentral on substantial alignment with Vv 7 (§0.1–11.1) and Vv 8 (§0.1–10.4), in addition to complete verse commentary coverage in the *Vimānavatthu-aṭṭhakathā* (§1.1–10.4) [DharmaNexus]. Formulaic verses praising divine beauty and heavenly vehicles also link the text to other *Vimānavatthu* poems, such as *Guttilavimānavatthu* (Vv 33), *Catutthapīṭhavimānavatthu* (Vv 4), and *Tatiyapīṭhavimānavatthu* (Vv 3) [DharmaNexus]. No cross-language alignments with Chinese, Sanskrit, or Tibetan collections are reported [DharmaNexus].
*No discussion of this text was found in the reference-literature corpus; the overview relies on SuttaCentral and DharmaNexus data.*
